newsitem.title: JAPAN: Forming steps for Japan stocks hard-bankers' chief.
newsitem.headline: Forming steps for Japan stocks hard-bankers' chief.

text.p: Formulating specific measures to boost share prices across the board on the Tokyo stock market would be difficult and individual companies must make efforts to improve their business situations, Shunsaku Hashimoto, chairman of the Federation of Bankers Associations of Japan, said on Tuesday.
Japanese banks were not planning to seek government money to solve their bad-loan problems, Hashimoto told a news conference.
He also said that it was necessary to implement Japan's financial "Big Bang" sooner than the government's 2001 target.
Hashimoto, who is president of Sakura Bank Ltd, also said that his bank's earnings in the year to March 31 would not be hurt by the current level of Tokyo share prices.
He said privatising Japan's postal savings system was an important option in restructuring Japan's posts and telecommunications.

Tokyo's stock market has been especially sluggish since December. The market's key index, the Nikkei average of 225 leading shares, ended at 17,796.57 on Tuesday, up 461.67 points or 2.66 percent from Monday's close.
Sakura said in November that it expected to post parent current profit of 90 billion yen in the year to March 31, against a current loss of 382.27 billion yen the previous year.
